reuse.why: Routes getScheduledAmount through a new getPlannedAmount and reuses getApproxNumberThreshold, but four server/shared sites keep their own dispatch instead of calling the existing getScheduledAmount that already handles missing/number/range.

duplication.why: The missing/number/range ternary survives at updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions, and the template keeps its own op check, each calling getPlannedAmount only for part of the decision.

placement.why: The rule sits in shared/schedules.ts and expectedAmount is computed in scheduleModel.toExternal, but adding an output-only optional field to the input-shaped APIScheduleEntity type mixes request and response shapes.

scope.why: Edits stay on amount sites, the helper, the API model, tests and release notes.

maintainability.why: Three overlapping entry points (getRangeAmount, getPlannedAmount, getScheduledAmount with inverse then op), stale comments ('end furthest from zero') and call sites whose numeric branch skips the approximate rule make the rule easy to break and already inconsistent between paths.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts updateActions and postTransactionForSchedule, shared/schedules.ts computeSchedulePreviewTransactions and server/budget/schedule-template.ts createScheduleList keep their own dispatch instead of calling getScheduledAmount/getPlannedAmount for the whole decision; the numeric branch at the app.ts and preview sites never applies the approximate rule.

disguised_duplication.where: The retained dispatches are the original ternaries with only the range branch swapped, visible rather than reshaped.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gained an op parameter after inverse; updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule, computeSchedulePreviewTransactions and the template's createScheduleList bypass it with their own number/range/op dispatch.
